posts.title: I built a self-healing open-source system that routes 70% of revenue to Gaza humanitarian aid
posts.content:
Hey r/solarpunk,

I've been building what I call SolarPunk -- an autonomous digital organism that generates revenue through digital art and products, then routes 70% of every dollar to Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF).

The system has 422 engines and 158 neurons. It self-heals, self-wires new connections, and runs entirely on GitHub Actions for $0/month. Everything is public. Every transaction is logged in a public ledger.

The core idea: what if mutual aid infrastructure was forkable? Anyone can clone this repo and aim it at whatever crisis they care about -- Sudan, Congo, their local community.

The art gallery sells $1 prints with 70% going to PCRF (4-star Charity Navigator rating for 12 consecutive years). No middlemen.

- Repo: https://github.com/meekotharaccoon-cell/meeko-nerve-center
- Art gallery: https://meekotharaccoon-cell.github.io/gaza-rose-gallery
- PCRF: https://www.pcrf.net

Looking for feedback, forks, and people who want to build mutual aid infrastructure that actually works.

posts.title: 422-engine autonomous system that self-heals and routes revenue to humanitarian aid -- fully open source
posts.content:
Sharing a project I've been working on: a self-sustaining digital organism built entirely with open-source tools.

**What it does:**
- 422 engines handle everything from content generation to crisis monitoring
- 158 neural pathways connect the engines into a nervous system
- Self-healing: if an engine breaks, the system detects and repairs it
- Self-wiring: new engines get automatically connected to the nervous system
- Runs on GitHub Actions -- $0/month hosting cost

**The mission:** 70% of all revenue goes to Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF). The system sells $1 digital art prints through a GitHub Pages storefront with PayPal and BTC payments. No platform middlemen.

**Why I'm sharing:** This architecture is fully forkable. Someone could clone it and point it at any cause -- local mutual aid, environmental monitoring, disaster relief. The infrastructure doesn't care what mission you give it.

Tech stack: Python, GitHub Actions, JSON state management, zero external dependencies beyond Git.

Repo: https://github.com/meekotharaccoon-cell/meeko-nerve-center

Would love technical feedback. PRs welcome.

posts.title: Built forkable open-source infrastructure that automatically generates and routes funds to PCRF for Gaza
posts.content:
I wanted to share a project focused on making mutual aid infrastructure that anyone can replicate.

The system is called SolarPunk. It's an autonomous digital organism that:

- Sells $1 digital art prints through its own storefront (no Etsy/platform fees)
- Routes 70% of every dollar to Palestine Children's Relief Fund
- Tracks every transaction in a public ledger for full transparency
- Runs for free on GitHub Actions

PCRF has a 4-star Charity Navigator rating for 12 consecutive years. They're providing medical care and surgery to children in Gaza right now.

The important part: **this is forkable.** If you have a cause you care about, you can clone the entire system and aim it at that cause. The 422 engines handle content generation, outreach, crisis monitoring, and revenue routing.

Art gallery (every print is $1): https://meekotharaccoon-cell.github.io/gaza-rose-gallery
Full system repo: https://github.com/meekotharaccoon-cell/meeko-nerve-center

Happy to answer questions about the architecture or help anyone fork it for their community.
